title: I Took the College Lab Safety Form to the TA Who Skipped Goggles

parts.text: I put on scratched goggles at 2:10 because the syllabus said no exceptions. The TA, Connor, wore none and leaned over my beaker to "check." I was nineteen. Acid is not a vibe. I asked him to follow the form we all signed. He said TAs are trained. A drop hit the bench paper and fumed. I photographed the fume, his uncovered eyes, the signed form on the door. Then he marked my pre-lab late because I had asked the question out loud.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He dinged my pre-lab for asking him to cover his eyes over acid.

social.video_title: The TA skipped goggles and graded my caution — Part 1/2
social.description: Scratched plastic, a fuming drop, trained but uncovered. Then a late mark. Would you have closed the beaker?

parts.text: I emailed the lab coordinator the photo and the late mark. Connor got a reminder and a pair of goggles that fit. My pre-lab score came back. The bench paper was changed. I still hate the smell. I like my corneas. Trained means the form, not a face over a beaker. The syllabus kept being right. Nineteen is not too young to want eyes.

social.video_title: The coordinator returned the points and the plastic — Part 2/2
social.description: Goggles on the TA, score restored, fume gone. Was a title PPE?
